customary: done traditionally or according to established habit
It is customary in the village to greet elders with a small bow.
rights: things a person or group is legally or morally entitled to
The new law expanded workers' rights to paid leave.
whole: Within a few generations, the whole structure lost its foundation.
arrangement: a plan or agreement made in advance
They reached an arrangement to share the cost of repairs equally.
rested: relaxed after effort, or leaned on something
She rested for an hour before continuing the hike.
institutions: plural of institution: large, established organisations
Strong institutions help a country recover quickly from a crisis.
took: past tense of take; obtained, seized, or required something
Computers took the jobs we thought were hardest, and left the ones a child can do.
hundred: He paid a hundred dollars for the used bicycle.
years: Somebody must own the roof and repaint it every few years.
build: to construct something by putting parts together
They plan to build a new library in the town centre.
rebuilt: built again after being damaged or destroyed
The cathedral was rebuilt stone by stone after the fire.
schedule: a plan of when tasks or events will happen
The train schedule changes slightly during public holidays.
removed: The stubborn stain was finally removed with a strong cleaner.
problem: a matter that is difficult to deal with or solve
The main problem with the plan was its enormous cost.
but: used to introduce something contrasting with what has just been said
She wanted to stay longer, but the last train was leaving soon.
its: belonging to a thing, animal, or situation already mentioned
The cat licked its paw before curling up to sleep.
inevitability: the fact of being certain to happen
Investors began to accept the inevitability of a market correction.
description: a spoken or written account of something
The police asked for a detailed description of the missing dog.
happens: takes place; occurs, third person singular
It happens more often than people realise during exam season.
has: has; present tense of have, third person singular
The library has extended its opening hours during exam season.
no: not any; used to indicate a complete absence
There was no sound at all in the empty hall.
real: actually existing; genuine, not imagined or fake
The documentary tells the real story behind the famous painting.
condition: the state that something or someone is in
The old bridge is in poor condition and needs urgent repair.
law: a rule made by a government that people must obey
The new law requires all drivers to wear seatbelts.
human: relating to or characteristic of people
con người, thuộc về con người
The robot cannot yet match human judgment in complex situations.
nature: the basic or inherent character of a person or thing; the physical world
It is human nature to notice bad news more than good news.
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
thing: an object, idea, or matter not named specifically
There's one thing I still don't understand about the plan.
survives: continues to live or exist after a difficulty
The old tradition still survives in a few remote mountain villages.
turns: present tense of turn, used with he/she/it; changes direction
When the frame begins to lean to the left, the front wheel turns slightly to the left as well.
depend: to be affected by or determined by something
Your success in this course will depend on regular practice.
built: constructed, past tense and participle of build
The bridge was built over a hundred years ago and still stands today.
